title: Scaffold a Go App
bottom_line: Type one command, answer a few questions, and Claude writes, builds and tests a Go web app. Fill in `.env`, migrate, then run `make dev`.

sections.heading: One command starts a new Go web app

blocks.caption: Both flags are optional. Without them the app targets Railway and uses the AI model openai/gpt-4o-mini.

blocks.text: The skill scaffolds a complete Go web application skeleton. **Scaffolding** means writing the starting files and folders of a new project. It is the Go counterpart of `fastapi-template`, with the same features, env var names and frontend, and no Python anywhere.

cards.title: Name the app
cards.text: `/go-webapp-template:go-webapp-template create a new app called my-app`

cards.title: Add flags
cards.text: `/go-webapp-template:go-webapp-template [--host railway|generic] [--ai-model <openrouter model id>]`. The defaults are railway and openai/gpt-4o-mini.

cards.title: Just describe it
cards.text: Say what you want in plain words, for example: "Scaffold a new Go web app with HTMX for a task management tool".

blocks.text: Claude also uses this skill on its own when you ask for a new Go web app, to scaffold a Go project, start a Go server, Go + HTMX, a golang backend, a net/http app with templates, or anything about bootstrapping a Go web application from scratch. If you ask for Python/FastAPI, Claude uses fastapi-template instead.
The plugin needs no environment variables and has no plugin settings. Its second skill, fastapi-go-migration, migrates existing fastapi-template projects to this stack in place.

sections.heading: Two flags change where it deploys and which AI model it uses

rows: With `generic`, the skill leaves out `Procfile`, `railpack.json`, the `internal/wake` package, the Railway pre-deploy command `./out migrate up`, and the Railway deploy instructions.
The default AI model the app sends requests to through OpenRouter.

blocks.text: With `--host generic` you deploy the `./out` binary to any host. The app still reads `PORT` and its connection strings from the environment. Migrations then run by hand (`./out migrate up` against the production `ENGINE_URL`) or in the host's release step.

blocks.title: Opinionated defaults and how to change them
rows: Deploy to Railway: `Procfile`, `railpack.json`, the `internal/wake` package that retries a sleeping Railway database or Redis, and `./out migrate up` as Railway's pre-deploy command
`--host generic` (then run `./out migrate up` by hand or in your host's release step)
AI calls go to OpenRouter with the model `openai/gpt-4o-mini`
Server listens on port 8000 in the main checkout, `8000+N` in each `claude --worktree` checkout
`PORT` in `.env` or the environment, or `make dev PORT=<port>`

sections.heading: Claude asks three questions, then writes, builds and tests the app

steps.title: The app name
steps.text: Claude asks for the app name in kebab-case (lowercase words joined by hyphens) if you did not give one. It is also the Go module path. The display name in pages is the Title Case of it (`my-app` becomes `My App`) unless you give one.

steps.title: Which features to include
steps.text: Claude confirms which optional parts go in: the database, AI through OpenRouter, and Redis caching. The defaults are in the table below.

steps.title: Where to put it
steps.text: Claude asks for the target directory. The default is the current directory.

steps.title: Files are generated
steps.text: Claude writes all the files, then copies `.env.example` to `.env` (which git ignores) so `make dev` works out of the box.

steps.title: It builds and tests the app
steps.text: Claude runs these checks in the new folder. `go mod tidy` may raise the `go` version line in `go.mod`; that is expected.

block.code: go mod tidy && gofmt -l . && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...

blocks.title: Optional features and their defaults
rows: yes if AI is included, otherwise ask

sections.heading: You get a full Go project with server, pages and database

blocks.title: The stack inside the generated app
rows: PostgreSQL via pgx/v5 + goose SQL migrations (embedded, run by the server binary)
Railway (Procfile + `railpack.json` with an explicit `go build -o out ./cmd/server`) by default; with `--host generic`, none of the Railway files or wake-up code

terms.definition: The programming language the whole app is written in.
A small library that lets links and forms fetch new HTML from the server without reloading the page.
A small library for interface behaviour that stays in the browser, such as opening a menu.
A file that changes the database structure; goose applies them in order.
A fast in-memory store, used here as a cache.
A service that forwards AI requests to many AI models through one API key.
A hosting service, the default place the app deploys to.
The single program file the build produces, here called `./out`.

blocks.title: What the generated app already does
items: Every link and form navigates without a full-page reload (hx-boost on the page body), which matters most when the app is wrapped with Capacitor.
A failed request (server error, network/offline, timeout) shows the user visible feedback instead of leaving the page looking stuck.
Logins and other per-user state are kept in signed cookies, keyed by `SESSION_SECRET`.
Missing required environment variables make the app fail at startup, not on the first request.
`DEV_MODE=ON` gives DEBUG logging, cookies that work on http://localhost, a `-dev` cache prefix, and template/CSS edits that show without a rebuild.
With host `railway`, a sleeping Railway Postgres or Redis is woken up before use.
Migrations are built into the server binary: `make migrate-up` locally, `make migrate-create name=add_users` for a new migration file. The deploy image has only the binary (no `make`).
AI answers are cached in Redis.

blocks.title: Generated structure
blocks.code:
<app-name>/
├── cmd/server/main.go       # serve, or `migrate up|down|status|create <name>`
├── cmd/worktree-env/main.go # per-worktree port, DB and Redis
├── .claude/settings.json    # hooks that run worktree-env
├── embed.go                 # embeds templates/, static/, migrations/
├── internal/
│   ├── config/
│   ├── wake/                # ping-with-retry for a sleeping Railway DB/Redis (railway host only)
│   ├── auth/                # signed cookies
│   ├── db/                  # pgxpool, goose, example queries
│   ├── cache/
│   ├── ai/
│   └── server/              # routes, middleware, errors, rendering, tests
├── migrations/
├── templates/
│   ├── base.html
│   ├── index.html
│   └── prompts/
├── static/
├── go.mod
├── Makefile
├── Procfile                 # railway host only (the default)
├── .env.example
└── .gitignore
blocks.caption: The wake folder and the Procfile only appear with the default railway host.

sections.heading: Have these ready before you run the generated app

cards.title: Go
cards.text: The generated `go.mod` says `go 1.26`; Go 1.21 or newer downloads that toolchain automatically. The code itself needs 1.22+ for its route patterns.

cards.title: make
cards.text: For the `make dev`, `make test` and migration targets.

cards.title: PostgreSQL and Redis
cards.text: A PostgreSQL database and a Redis server, when those parts are included.

cards.title: OpenRouter API key
cards.text: Needed when the AI part is included.

cards.title: Railway account
cards.text: For deploying with the default host.

sections.heading: Fill in .env, apply migrations, then start the server

steps.title: Go into the project
steps.text: Open a terminal in the new folder.

steps.title: Set up your .env file
steps.text: Copy the example settings file, then edit `.env` with real values (see the table below). The skill already made this copy when it generated the files.

steps.title: Start the dev server
steps.text: The app is now running at localhost:8000.

block.code: make dev          # start dev server at localhost:8000

blocks.title: Environment variables the generated app reads from .env
Quick Start in one block
blocks.code:
cd <app-name>
cp .env.example .env
# edit .env with real values
go mod tidy
make migrate-up   # apply migrations
make dev          # start dev server at localhost:8000
make test         # go test ./...

sections.heading: Each Claude worktree gets its own port, database and Redis

blocks.text: When you work in a `claude --worktree` checkout, a hook gives it its own `.env`: a port of `8000+N` (the main checkout stays on 8000), a Postgres database `<app_name>_wtN` with migrations applied, and Redis db `N`. Slots run from 1 to 9. So `make dev` can run in the main checkout and in every worktree at once.

rows: Set up this worktree by hand: write its `.env`, create its database and migrate it. Does nothing in the main checkout or if `.env` exists.
Drop the database and flush the Redis db of worktrees that no longer exist. The hooks also run this when a session starts or ends.

blocks.text: The main database and Redis db 0 are never touched.

sections.heading: Production migrations need one setup step from you

cards.title: Railway host (default)
cards.text: Set `./out migrate up` as the service's pre-deploy command in the Railway dashboard (Settings → Deploy → Pre-deploy Command) so it runs on every deploy.

cards.title: Generic host
cards.text: Run `./out migrate up` against the production `ENGINE_URL` yourself, or in your host's release step.

blocks.title: Run the migration by hand on Railway

sections.heading: Replace the example parts with your own

blocks.caption: After generating, Claude reminds you of these steps.

cards.title: Replace the example table
cards.text: Delete the example `internal/db/items.go` and `migrations/00001_create_items.sql`, then run `make migrate-create name=<first_table>` and write real SQL.

cards.title: Railway pre-deploy command
cards.text: With a database and host `railway`: open the service → Settings → Deploy → Pre-deploy Command and set `./out migrate up` before the first deploy.

points.text: This skill uses no `railway.json` (config-as-code), so you set it in the dashboard.

cards.title: Generic host migrations
cards.text: With a database and host `generic`: run `./out migrate up` by hand or in the host's release step on every deploy.

cards.title: Start the server
cards.text: Run `make dev` to start the dev server.

sections.heading: Example: a recipe app for any host

before.label: You type
before.text: `/go-webapp-template:go-webapp-template create a new app called recipe-box --host generic`

blocks.code: /go-webapp-template:go-webapp-template create a new app called recipe-box --host generic

blocks.text: Follow the Quick Start steps above, then build with `go build -o out ./cmd/server` and run `./out` on your host.
